page: Microsoft Azure M32bs_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the MBSMediumMemoryv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8473C processor with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. The processor includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 105 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, relying instead on external block storage.

Benchmark results show strong performance in specific single-threaded and multi-threaded operations. The server achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2210.0 and a multi-core score of 18347.0, both placing in the strong category. Gzip compression single-threaded throughput reached 33.05 GB/sec, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression registered at 210.74 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput is also strong at 53.69 GB/sec. In contrast, database operations and memory bandwidth tests, such as the large block read-only bandwidth of 182.67 GB/sec, fall within the average tier.

The hardware configuration presents distinct performance tradeoffs. While text generation for small language models (135M parameters) is highly efficient at 343.5 tokens/sec, text generation for large models (70B parameters) drops to a weak 2.74 tokens/sec due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average database operation benchmarks, this server is configured for memory-intensive workloads, software compilation, image processing, and web serving, rather than large-scale LLM execution or local-storage-dependent database tasks.
